items.title: Ray Bryant interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: It goes all the way back to the St. Louis Blues, Bessie Smith, and it was definitely a production of the black culture here in the United States

ctx.x: Is it possible to put into words what is so attractive — I don’t know if that’s the right word — but the blues just seems to grab people. Have you ever been able to understand why that is?

Not really. I guess it was one of the — it was the first form. Blues, and then jazz. It was definitely one of the more common harmonic structures for jazz tunes. It goes all the way back to the St. Louis Blues, Bessie Smith, and it was definitely a production of the black culture here in the United States, it’s the blues. And jazz I guess — the main players of this music were black people, and it’s just like the blues is like the music of our people. It’s infectious, everybody likes the blues, but nobody wants to…
Has jazz been instrumental in helping the racial scene in this country?
